The Federal Government has graduated 87,701 beneficiaries of its first cohort of the Technical and Vocational Education and Training programme and enrolled another 150,000 Nigerians for the second cohort. As reported by Nairametrics, the Minister of Education, Dr Tunji Alausa, disclosed this on Wednesday during the graduation ceremony of the first cohort and the presentation of starter kits to beneficiaries in Abuja. Alausa said the 150,000 trainees were selected from nearly 1.5 million applications received for the second cohort and would undergo training at 82 accredited centres across the country. According to him, the programme is designed to bridge the gap between skills acquisition and economic opportunities by equipping beneficiaries with practical knowledge and tools to establish businesses or secure employment. He said Nigeria’s development depended on building a skilled workforce capable of meeting the demands of industries and society, particularly in technical and vocational fields. He added that competency-based assessments and certification were ongoing to ensure beneficiaries obtained nationally recognised skills qualifications. Alausa described the distribution of starter kits as a critical component of the programme, saying access to the necessary equipment would enable graduates to translate their skills into productive economic activities. Earlier, the Minister of State for Education, Prof. Suwaiba Ahmad, described the graduation as a significant milestone in the Federal Government’s efforts to reposition technical and vocational education in Nigeria. Ahmad said the programme had demonstrated the government’s capacity to provide practical training, stipends and starter kits to empower young Nigerians. She recalled that the initiative initially faced doubts over the government’s ability to pay trainees’ stipends, remunerate service providers and provide starter kits. However, she said the programme had since become a reality, adding that its structure was designed to align vocational training with industry requirements through accredited centres and relevant curricula. Also speaking, the Chairman of the House of Representatives Committee on Basic Education, Mark Useni, described technical and vocational education as fundamental to Nigeria’s technological advancement. The TVET programme is part of the Federal Government’s efforts to equip Nigerians with practical skills, promote entrepreneurship and expand employment opportunities through vocational education.
